name: registry
summary: Lazy-loaded extensible collection with controlled access: registry, event, handler, provider.
description: Creates the four-part registry pattern: registry storage, initiated event, core-items handler, and provider service
problem: You have an extensible collection of related items (currencies, resolvers, integrations) that third parties should be able to add to — but only through a controlled surface — and that should cost nothing until first accessed. You need lazy loading at both the registry and item level, with the storage mechanism protected from direct manipulation.
appliesWhen: Third parties or other modules need to register items into a shared collection
You want precise control over which operations (add, get, remove) extenders may perform
Items are expensive to build and should instantiate lazily on first access
Items are registered at runtime rather than wired statically in the container
avoidWhen: The collection is fixed and internal — a plain array or DI bindings are simpler
You need per-item configuration values, not extensible items — that's a provider
Consumers need write access to a shared mutable state bag — registries are not global state containers
Only one implementation of a behavior is being selected — that's a strategy
examples: Add a currency registry third parties can extend
I need a lazily-loaded catalog of integrations
Let plugins register their own field resolvers, but not delete ours
Create an extensible registry of report types
tradeoffs: Four files plus a listener registration — the heaviest core pattern. Buys controlled extensibility and two-level lazy loading; skip it for fixed internal collections. The event's method surface is the security boundary: only expose the operations extenders should have.
outputs: A {name}Registry class using WithGet/WithSet for lazy item storage
A {name}RegistryInitiatedEvent exposing the controlled registration surface
A RegisterCore{name}Items handler that seeds core items on first access
A {name}Provider service that lazily initializes and reads the registry
A listener registration mapping the event to the handler in the initializer
postApply: Seed core items in RegisterCore{name}Items::handle() using $event->set(key, fn () => ...)
Replace {name}Provider::get() with purpose-specific, typed accessors for the item type
Expose only the operations third parties should have on the event (omit delete to forbid deletion)
Inject {name}Provider wherever items are consumed — never touch the registry directly
Confirm the listener wiring via `phpnomad inspect:di`

name.description: Domain name for the registry (e.g. Currency)
name.aiHint: Singular PascalCase domain concept, no suffix — the recipe derives {name}Registry, {name}Provider, etc. (Currency, FieldResolver, Integration).

eventId.description: Unique event identifier for the registry initiated event (e.g. currency.registry.initiated)
eventId.aiHint: Lowercase, dot-separated, ending in 'registry.initiated' ({nameSnake}.registry.initiated). Must be unique across the project.

initializer.description: FQCN of the initializer to register the listener in
initializer.aiHint: Pick the initializer that owns this domain. If unsure, use the project's root initializer.
